company_research.industry: Food and Beverage Manufacturing, FMCG Manufacturing
recent_news: McCain Foods is investing $3.75 million in a partnership led by the McKenna Institute at the University of New Brunswick (UNB) to advance digital agriculture and regenerative farming practices. This includes establishing a Chair in Digital Agriculture at UNB.

McCain Foods launched Presia Ag Insights, a new business unit developed from a decade of collaboration and the acquisition of predictive crop portfolio technologies from Resson. Presia aims to support farmers in building operational resilience and adopting regenerative agricultural practices.

McCain Foods has expanded its Innovation Hub farms across North America, adding four new locations to accelerate research into sustainable and regenerative agriculture practices. This is part of their goal to implement regenerative agriculture across 100% of their global potato acreage by 2030.
McCain Foods has established three 'Farms of the Future' across diverse growing regions (Canada, South Africa, UK) as commercial-scale research sites for regenerative agriculture.
culture_signals: Values and culture are at the heart of everything they do.

additional_context: McCain Foods is a family-owned business founded in 1957, and is the world's largest manufacturer of frozen potato products. They operate 54 production facilities on six continents and generate annual sales exceeding $14 billion CAD.
The company is committed to implementing regenerative agriculture across 100% of its global potato acreage by 2030.
McCain Foods is actively using data-backed solutions and digital technologies to scale sustainable agriculture, integrating agricultural data, consumer transparency, and financial innovation.

The Digital Agriculture Analytics Lead role focuses on translating agricultural and operational challenges into actionable insights using advanced analytics and AI, with an emphasis on decision impact, adoption, and measurable business value.
The company partners with approximately 3,500 to 4,400 farmers globally.
